svg.title: PGD-3 as a subset of FGSM, and the held-out matched contrasts
svg.desc: Panel A: schematic showing that after 8-bit rounding PGD-3 keeps FGSM's sign on coordinates where all three step signs agree and is zero elsewhere. Panel B: per-group held-out contrasts, PGD-3 subset minus random subset (mean +6.50) and top-gradient subset minus random subset (mean -1.38).
svg.text: 8-bit rounding turns PGD-3 into a subset of FGSM
Schematic: six RGB-channel coordinates, illustrative values
Steps of ε/4 never reach the ε-ball boundary, so each displacement is ±¼ε or ±¾ε.
Rounding to the 8-bit grid (spacing ε) sends ±¼ε to 0 and ±¾ε to ±ε.
A coordinate survives only if all three step signs agree, and it then carries
FGSM's sign (shaded). The compared masks (PGD-3, random, top-|∇|) each keep k of
FGSM's coordinates at one level with FGSM's own sign there; only the choice of
coordinates differs, so overall counts of + and − can differ between masks.
48 independent scene groups; difference in margin drop, logits
Margin-drop difference (logits); right = more damage than random
Dots: one per scene group, averaged over the two source contexts; random = mean of 8 seeds.
Bar: mean and 95% percentile bootstrap CI over groups (9,999 draws), from the frozen analysis.
Within each source context, PGD-3's subset beat all 8 random subsets in 48 of 48 groups.
